LEARNING PATH LESSON · SIGHT WORDS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Blue — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

Five minutes, one card: say “blue” clearly, use it in a real sentence (“The sky is blue.”) and finish with one small game.

What it means

It names the color of the sky on a clear day.

How to teach it

  1. Hold up the card and read “blue” slowly, sliding a finger under it. Point out its shape: a b, an l and a u, and a silent e at the end.
  2. Cover the word with a hand and ask your child to say it from memory. Draw a big tick on the canvas when they get it.
  3. Play the game below, say “blue” one last time and stop while it is still fun.

How to say it

Say bloo, like glue and shoe.

Where to use it

Say it in a real sentence: “The sky is blue.” Then try “I like blue.” Where to spot it: the sky, the sea and blueberries.

Try this game

Point to something blue in the room and say blue. Collect three blue things and line them up.

Understanding check

Ask your child to find something in the room that fits “blue”, then to read the card without help.

Parent tips

If “blue” slips away overnight, that is normal. Bring it back the next day with the same game and a smile.

This lesson pairs with the Blue flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Sight Words (Class 29).
